episodes.title: The Optic Disc: Cup, Rim & the ISNT Rule Explained
episodes.description:
Are you reading the optic disc as carefully as your patients deserve? In this clinical episode of Focus Cast, we go deep on one of the most underread structures in routine optometric practice — the optic nerve head. Designed exclusively for licensed optometrists, residents, and eye care professionals, this episode breaks down the anatomy of the optic cup and neuroretinal rim, explains why the cup-to-disc ratio alone is not enough, and shows you exactly how to apply the ISNT rule at the slit lamp to catch the earliest signs of glaucomatous damage before your patient loses a single degree of visual field.

We cover the normal neuroretinal rim thickness pattern, why inferior notching is your earliest red flag, and how violations of the ISNT rule should immediately shape your clinical thinking. You will also get a practical differential diagnosis that separates glaucomatous optic neuropathy from AION, compressive optic neuropathy, optic neuritis, and large physiologic cups — because not every suspicious disc is glaucoma.

From chairside decision-making to OCT interpretation, pachymetry, 24-2 visual field analysis, and risk-stratified monitoring schedules, this episode gives you a complete, evidence-based clinical framework you can apply starting with your very next patient. We also discuss when to refer, how to document your reasoning, and which patient populations carry the highest glaucoma risk.

If you want to sharpen your optic nerve evaluation skills and build more confident, defensible clinical decisions around glaucoma suspects, this episode is essential listening. Subscribe to Focus Cast and visit focuslinks.in for more clinical episodes built specifically for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: Fundus Photography: Fields, Stereo Pairs & Montage Techniques
episodes.description:
Are you capturing fundus images or building true clinical documents? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down the diagnostic art and science behind fundus photography composition — a skill every optometrist needs to master to catch the pathology a single frame can miss.

We start with ETDRS field definitions, the standardized anatomical zones that form the foundation of every meaningful posterior segment image. You will learn why field selection is a clinical decision, not a default setting, and how choosing the wrong fields in a diabetic patient can leave peripheral hemorrhages completely undocumented.

From there, we move into fundus montage construction — how overlapping fields by twenty to thirty percent eliminates blind spots and creates the panoramic view essential for detecting lattice degeneration, peripheral retinal breaks, and retinoschisis in high myopes and at-risk patients. We walk through real clinical scenarios, including a high myope with a horseshoe tear hiding beyond the posterior pole, to show exactly what is at stake when peripheral imaging is skipped.

We also cover stereo fundus photography, an underutilized technique that restores the depth perception critical for evaluating glaucomatous disc cupping, choroidal nevi elevation, and subretinal fluid — clinical distinctions that flat images simply cannot reliably convey.

Finally, we tie it all together with a practical chairside decision-making framework: how to let your clinical question drive your imaging protocol, how to document methodology for co-management, and when peripheral findings cross the threshold from watch-and-educate to urgent retinal referral.

If you are ready to stop taking snapshots and start creating diagnostic records that protect your patients and elevate your practice, this episode is for you. Visit Focuslinks dot in for more clinical resources built exclusively for eye care professionals.
